---
title: "Assigning NULL to a list element deletes it"
ref: LEN-06
categories: [Empty and NA]
impact: silencieux
attendu: "the list keeps `threshold`, with an empty value"
versions: "All"
source: "Slack ThinkR (2022), The R Inferno"
---

::: {.piege}
```{r}
settings <- list(threshold = 10, colour = "red")
settings$threshold <- NULL
str(settings)
```
:::

## Why

For a list, `l$a <- NULL` (like `l[["a"]] <- NULL`) is the way to delete an element. It is not a value assignment: the element disappears, along with its name, and the list gets shorter.

When `NULL` is a legitimate value (a setting "left blank", a default argument), the code believes it stored it, and the key no longer exists. The positions of the following elements shift too.

## The fix

Assign a list containing `NULL`, with single brackets.

::: {.piege}
```{r}
settings <- list(threshold = 10, colour = "red")
settings["threshold"] <- list(NULL)
str(settings)
```
:::
